sources.note: Nothing on phonology; classification 'Sino-Tibetan, Tibeto-Burman, Burmic, Ngwi (Loloish), Northern', closest language Samatao; 3,300 speakers; written literature/recordings field left blank.

sources.citation: 何炳坤 [He Bingkun] (云南省民语委办公室). 2007. 云南民族语言调查 [Minority-language surveys in Yunnan]. 彝学研究网 (yixueyanjiu.com), posted 2007-01-07.
sources.note: No phonology content for Chesu. Relevant passage (original): '为了规范彝文，办公室的同志深入到禄劝、新平、石屏、弥勒、罗平、双柏、江城、墨江等彝族聚居县，收集了大量的彝族语言文字资料。当时境内彝族有240万，分为诺苏、纳苏、聂苏、罗武、…、勒苏、撒苏、车苏、民期、希期、纳若、撒马都、米西苏等34个支系… 许多语言资料虽然只以研究材料性质汇编成册，但仍然具有文献价值' — documents that data for Yi subgroups incl. Chesu were collected from 1983 and compiled as internal research volumes (work 2); nothing on tone or stress.

sources.citation: 龙倮贵 [Long Luogui]. 2007. 红河彝族族源族称及其人口分布 [Origins, ethnonyms and population distribution of the Yi of Honghe Prefecture]. 彝学研究网 (yixueyanjiu.com); Internet Archive copy 2017-12-22. (Source of the autonym 吉输颇 tɕi21su55pho21 in en.wikipedia 'Chesu language'.)
sources.note: Nothing: the 吉输颇 paragraph is tribal history; the only phonetic content is the autonym with tone letters. Searched the saved text for 声调/重音/音系: no hit relating to 吉输颇 or 车苏.

sources.citation: 巫达 [Wu Da]. 2002. 彝族与彝族群——从国家语文政策在彝族群中的实施谈起 [The Yi and the Yi groups: on the implementation of state language policy among Yi groups]. 彝族人网 yizuren.com, 2002-08-18 (section 二 summarises 云南省民族事务委员会研究室 1955《云南民族识别参考资料》).
sources.note: No phonology. Only a lexicostatistic note (original Chinese): '还有一个自称出枢巴的群体，他称车苏，人口约360余人。识别组把车苏语与聂苏彝语进行了比较，在712个词汇中，相同相近的有521个，占73.1%,语法结构相似，因此，证明车苏也是彝族的一个支系。' (A group calling itself Chushuba, called Chesu by others, ~360 people; compared with Niesu Yi: of 712 words 521 (73.1%) same or similar, grammar similar, so Chesu is a Yi branch.) Nothing on tone or stress.

sources.citation: Hattaway, Paul. 2000. Operation China: Introducing all the Peoples of China. Pasadena, CA: Piquant. Profile 'Chesu', p. 101 (one-page profile PDF republished by Asia Harvest; population source '6,350 (1998 J. Pelkey)').
sources.note: No phonology content. Language paragraph in full: 'Although the Chesu claim their language is not a Yi language, preliminary studies suggest it belongs to the Southern Yi language group and is similar to the Lesu language. Few Chesu are able to understand Mandarin Chinese.' Sidebar: 'Language: Sino-Tibetan, Tibeto-Burman, Burmese-Lolo, Lolo, Northern Lolo, Yi, Southern Yi; Dialects: 0'.

Nothing on stress.
